article_title: IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems
citation: Shwetha Singaravelu, Gayathri Muruganantham, Lakshmi Rajendran, Santhosh Sivasubramani. (2026). IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23322
title: IKS-Instruct dataset
description: IKS-Instruct is a released dataset of instruction-response pairs for teaching language models Indian Knowledge Systems pedagogy. The paper presents "a dataset of 24,795 instruction-response pairs for teaching language models to deliver educational content grounded in Indian Knowledge Systems (IKS)" spanning seven languages, 41 pedagogical techniques, and CBSE classes 6-12. Pairs come from six source categories and are stored in JSONL with structured metadata including source provenance, technique classification, language, subject, class level, and quality scores.
requirements: Pairs must pass the five-stage quality filtering pipeline including Teacher Fidelity scoring and multi-judge evaluation
constraints: Language distribution is imbalanced (English 36.1%, Malayalam 6.3%); CBSE alignment covers only classes 6-12; oral and manuscript-only traditions are not represented
target_learning_goals: IKS-grounded instruction across mathematics, science, social science, ethics, language, and AI/data science
examples: The released v1.9 dataset contains 24,795 pairs, with classical text corpus pairs the largest category at 27.5%
key_sources: Shwetha Singaravelu, Gayathri Muruganantham, Lakshmi Rajendran, Santhosh Sivasubramani. (2026). IKS-Instruct: A 24,000-Example Multilingual Dataset for Teaching Language Models Indian Knowledge Systems. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.23322

article_title: Using Sequence Analysis to Determine the Well-Functioning of Small Groups in Large Online Courses
citation: H. Ulrich Hoppe, et al. (2021). Using Sequence Analysis to Determine the Well-Functioning of Small Groups in Large Online Courses. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00229-9
title: IKARion system architecture: learning analytics backend with group model and rule-based adaptive scaffolding in Moodle
description: IKARion extends the Moodle platform with a dedicated learning analytics backend connected to an expert system for generating potentially adaptive scaffolds. "This architecture contains an analytics backend that analyzes the action logs received from the learning platform (Moodle) to generates a group model." The group model represents the current context of each learning group and instantiates variables such as inactivity (gaps), imbalance and productivity (word count), including a semantic word count based on a dictionary extracted from learning materials. The group model feeds a rule-based component that steers feedback and adaptation in Moodle; the learned decision tree provides "indicators for critical situations". Two consecutive versions were used in parallel with two versions of the CmC course and other smaller courses.
requirements: Connection to the Moodle learning platform supplying action logs in real time; the architecture "complies with the real-time requirement of the course settings"
constraints: The experiments with this architecture "did not exploit the potential of flexible adaptation"; scaffolds were triggered by clearly controlled and fixed conditions
target_learners: higher education students working in small groups in large online courses
target_learning_goals: improving collaboration and interaction in small-group work through timely feedback and scaffolding
examples: The IKARion architecture was used with two versions of the CmC course and other smaller courses, with scaffolds triggered by fixed conditions rather than flexible adaptation
key_sources: H. Ulrich Hoppe, et al. (2021). Using Sequence Analysis to Determine the Well-Functioning of Small Groups in Large Online Courses. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-020-00229-9
